priorities.question: Are the weak selected dips unusual under defensible correlation-preserving controls, and can signals of the measured depth survive the same selection procedure?
priorities.implementation: Freeze exact scope first. For96166003 reproduce original43/44 search; for469309982 reproduce the actual weak-seed/local-refinement selection, rather than borrow a global-search null threshold. Preserve full maxima/selection outcomes under fixed block lengths and deterministic draws. Pair with injected dips through identical preprocessing. Added sectors are opened data, never fresh holdouts. Use separate protocols per target.
priorities.decision: Frequent comparable null outcomes plus mixed followup can justify lower priority. Few exceedances only show conditional robustness; they do not establish a planet or survey FAP.
priorities.stop: One predeclared control matrix and report per target. No iterative choice of block lengths or omission of bad timing islands to rescue a result.

priorities.action: Conditional physical/binary compatibility on cached sector92
priorities.status: Assigned by coordinator to new_pass_review after recommendations; pending results.
priorities.question: Can the short roughly1.1percent event have a plausible target-host transit shape under explicit stellar, exposure, grazing and dilution assumptions; which binary alternatives remain?
priorities.implementation: Audit stellar inputs and cadence from existing files; fit exposure-integrated models using all five events with baselines, both saved detrendings and multi-start checks. Compare illustrative target and close-neighbor dilution assumptions. Do not assume uncertain photometric youth is established. Preserve local minima and physical assumptions.
priorities.decision: A physical inconsistency may deprioritize a specified host/model; a compatible transit only retains APC. No binary exclusion without an appropriate binary model or independent data.
priorities.stop: One declared comparison grid; no increasingly flexible models to force compatibility. If both interpretations fit, record degeneracy and defer.

priorities.action: Empirical source-model feasibility gate, before more host fits
priorities.status: conditional method-development avenue; not a ready validated test
priorities.question: Can data constrain image response independently enough to distinguish hosts when mission-PRF residuals and source rankings fail?
priorities.implementation: Audit cached stamps for useful out-of-event scene/pointing diversity and independently constrained nuisance response. Prespecify non-event training/validation splits; candidate events cannot tune response. Establish held-out residual performance and known-planet/contaminant controls before applying to either candidate. Isolated small stamps may not identify an empirical PRF; broader calibrated imagery would require separate scope.
priorities.decision: Proceed to candidate source comparison only if model adequacy and control host recovery improve on held-out data. A lower candidate fit residual alone is insufficient.
priorities.stop: One feasibility assessment and explicit go/no-go. If identifiability or control performance fails, stop image-model permutations and leave host unresolved.

priorities.question: Does an operational public route have securely associated, sufficiently useful epoch photometry for deep-blend alternatives?
priorities.implementation: Require evidence of an operational documented endpoint before retry. Query metadata/association first. If usable, freeze original timing-profile uncertainty, filters/cameras, source association and deep-eclipse sensitivity before flux access.
priorities.decision: May test deep contaminant eclipses; sparse or blended shallow non-detection is not exclusion.

priorities.implementation: Reuse current local snapshots first, join exact aliases and epochs, then make only missing metadata/literature checks with provenance. Do not repeat402358350 recent catalog searches without a changed database or new alias. No outreach.
priorities.decision: Known candidate identity or real resolved companion constraints can change novelty/physical interpretation. Catalog nonmatch cannot validate a planet.
